message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1968 | **Night of the Living Dead** (George A. Romero) | The original zombie film that defined a genre. |
| 1974 | **The Exorcist** | A chilling story of demonic possession that still feels fresh. |
| 1978 | **Halloween** (John Carpenter) | The birth of the slasher icon Michael Myers. |
| 1980 | **The Shining** (Stanley Kubrick) | A haunting psychological thriller set in an isolated hotel. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** (Wes Craven) | Freddy Krueger’s nightmare‑inducing terror. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** | A tense psychological thriller with unforgettable characters. |
| 1999 | **The Sixth Sense** | A twisty supernatural thriller that keeps you guessing. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (Danny Boyle) | A fast‑paced, post‑apocalyptic zombie film. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | A gritty, puzzle‑based horror that sparked a franchise. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Low‑budget found‑footage that made audiences jump at every creak. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (James Wan) | A modern supernatural horror that blends scares with a strong narrative. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and frightening. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | A unique, slow‑burning horror about an unstoppable curse. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | A period horror that uses atmosphere and dread over gore. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror that’s as smart as it is scary. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (John Krasinski) | Silence is the key to survival in this tense thriller. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** (Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that turns the sun into a source of dread. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** (Eliseo Subiela) | A modern retelling of the classic tale with a feminist twist. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** (Nia DaCosta) | A fresh take on a horror legend with strong social commentary. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** (Scott Derrickson) | A supernatural thriller that blends creepy atmosphere with a gripping plot. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** | A horror‑comedy about a killer doll that’s both funny and unsettling. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or found‑footage—and enjoy the chills!
